summary: The request check (PLAN-4 D16): a job submitted with `check: true` is held once its request is built - at its turn, by the application's build hook or the default one, so a request made from an earlier job's answer is seen as it will be sent - and waits, `held`, until it is sent or cancelled. This is what it holds: `request` exactly as it was built; `gen`, the parameters the queue would send it with (the job's own and its sampling hook's, the queue's own three - `model`, `n`, `retries` - never), and only those its model's engine reads: none for a whisper model, which reads its `fields` alone; the `model` and its `engine` (null: the server's backend does not say); the `messages` by role as the model will be asked them (a prompt is one user message), or, for a whisper model, the `audio` - its file and its length in seconds - and whisper-server's `fields`; `params`, every parameter the model will be sent, each with its `value` and where it came `from`: the `application` (the job or its sampling hook), the `model`'s settings (its sampling, and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` false for a model its settings tell not to think), or the `bootstrap`'s default (`max_tokens` 600) - anything no one names is llama-server's own; `count`, the request counted by its model against the context the model says it has, as a job's turn counts it (its model loaded for the count as a job's is, then left to its own idle clock), and whether it `fits` (a request that does not fit is held all the same, to be changed; sent unchanged, it fails `prompt_too_long` at its turn, counted again); `expect`, what the model's own statistics expect of it - the median and 90th percentile of its whole answers (`answer_s`), or, for audio, its length times the model's real-time factor - once the model has three measured; and `said`, in words, why any of these is not known. A held job is not running: the stall watch never takes it back, the coordinator's hang watch never counts it as work, and the queue's own pipeline does not keep the card for it - it waits for no one and nothing waits on the card for it. A job that is not held is refused `not_held`, with its status: one never marked, one not yet built, one already sent.
